title: Define canonical sources + versioning plan for Enterprise Security Enablement Kit v2
creator: Naomi Feldman
description:
Goal
Define (a) where the canonical “source of truth” for the enterprise security enablement kit lives, (b) how we version and approve changes, and (c) how we package/share field-ready artifacts without creating drift.

Background / problem
Security review materials are currently duplicated across Drive PDFs, email attachments, and old Confluence pages, leading to inconsistent answers during late-stage sales/procurement. Field also needs a single reliable link for “latest kit”, but we must control access for restricted evidence and avoid accidentally sharing internal-only guidance.

Deliverables in scope
1) Canonical location(s): where each asset lives as the source of truth.
2) Versioning scheme: document IDs, revision history, and how PDFs tie back to canonical content.
3) Quarterly update workflow: intake, drafting, review/approval, publication, and distribution.
4) Access model: what is customer-shareable vs internal-only, and how this is signposted.

Decision: Canonical sources
A. Confluence is canonical for customer-facing narrative content
- Canonical pages (customer-shareable):
  - Sales Enablement > Security FAQ > “Enterprise Security FAQ v2”
  - Security & Compliance > One-pagers (Data Residency, Data Retention Controls, Audit Logging Overview, SSO/SAML/SCIM, Secure SDLC, Incident Response & Notification)
  - Sales Enablement > “Standard RFP Response Library”
- Rationale: Confluence has stronger edit history + page restrictions + consistent linking for internal teams (Sales/SE/CS).

B. Google Drive PDFs are packaged exports (non-canonical)
- Drive contains:
  - Security FAQ v2 (PDF export)
  - One-pagers pack v2 (PDF export)
- Rule: Drive PDFs must include a footer stamp pointing back to the canonical Confluence page + version + last reviewed date. If there is a mismatch, Confluence wins.

C. Restricted evidence and SOPs remain internal-only
- Internal-only canonical pages (restricted):
  - Customer security review process SOP (evidence sharing, NDA requirements, who can share what)
  - Evidence pointer index (SOC 2 access flow, pen test summary pointers, subprocessor list pointers)
- Rule: No restricted artifacts live in the field-shareable Drive folder. Evidence is provided via the controlled process only.

Versioning plan (applies to FAQ, one-pagers, RFP library)
Version format
- Major.Minor (e.g., v2.0, v2.1)
- Major bump: material changes that affect customer interpretation or shared responsibility boundaries (e.g., new deployment mode guarantees, changes to retention defaults, changes to audit log scope).
- Minor bump: clarifications, formatting fixes, added Q&A, link updates, non-material corrections.

Required page metadata on Confluence (top-of-page block)
- Document name
- Version
- Owner
- Approvers (by role)
- Last reviewed date
- Next review due date
- Customer-shareable: Yes/No
- Notes: “If exported as PDF, this Confluence page is the source of truth.”

Change log requirements
- Maintain a dedicated changelog page for the Security FAQ (and a sectioned changelog for one-pagers pack + RFP library).
- Each entry must include: date, version, summary, approvers, and link to the Linear ticket/request.

PDF packaging requirements (Drive)
- Filename format:
  - Redwood-Inference_Enterprise-Security-FAQ_vX.Y_YYYY-MM-DD.pdf
  - Redwood-Inference_Compliance-One-Pagers_vX.Y_YYYY-MM-DD.pdf
- Footer stamp on every page:
  - “Redwood Inference | vX.Y | Last reviewed YYYY-MM-DD | Canonical: <Confluence link>”
- Distribution note on first page:
  - “Customer-shareable. For SOC 2 / pen test materials, request via Security Evidence Process (NDA may be required).”

Quarterly review + update workflow
Cadence
- Quarterly scheduled review (first two weeks of each quarter).
- Off-cycle updates allowed for urgent correctness (e.g., product behavior changes, incident-related wording updates, compliance scope change).

Intake
- Requests come via:
  - Linear ticket (preferred)
  - Slack escalation to #security-review-support for urgent clarifications (must be converted into a Linear ticket within 2 business days)
- Each request must include:
  - What asset(s) are affected (FAQ / which one-pager / RFP library)
  - Proposed wording (if available)
  - Reason (customer question, product change, compliance change)
  - Evidence pointer (if applicable)

Drafting
- Owner drafts directly in Confluence (not in Drive) using “draft mode” or restricted view until ready for review.
- For multi-asset changes, link a single parent ticket to sub-tasks per asset.

Review + approval (minimum set)
- Security Engineering approver: Marcus Lin (or delegate)
- GRC/compliance approver: Olga Petrov (or delegate)
- Product/PM approval: Naomi Feldman (ensures alignment to product reality and avoids over-commitments)
- Solutions Engineering reviewer: Markus Klein (ensures field usability / common objections are handled)
- Legal review only when:
  - The change materially impacts contractual language, notification commitments, or creates new “guarantee” statements.

Publication
- Once approved:
  - Update Confluence version + last reviewed date
  - Add changelog entry
  - Export PDFs and place into the designated Drive folder
  - Update “Latest kit” shortcut link (Drive shortcut + Confluence hub page)
  - Notify Sales/SE/CS via enablement channel with a short delta summary

Distribution + single “latest kit” link
- Confluence hub page is the canonical index: links to FAQ, one-pagers, RFP library, and the Drive folder for PDFs.
- Drive folder contains the latest PDFs plus an archive subfolder (read-only).
- Field guidance: share the Drive PDF links for convenience, but rely on Confluence for quoting language.

Access controls / classification
- Customer-shareable content:
  - FAQ v2, One-pagers (customer-facing), RFP response library (approved answers only)
- Internal-only content:
  - Evidence pointer index, customer security review SOP, any raw compliance artifacts (SOC 2 report, pen test report) unless explicitly approved for a given customer under the evidence process.
- All customer-shareable pages must be clearly marked “Customer-shareable” and avoid:
  - Mentioning internal tools/vendors not already in the public subprocessor list
  - Including customer names, incident details, or internal-only operational runbooks

Open questions (tracked here, not blockers)
- Whether we add SCIM language as “available in Enterprise plans” vs “supported” (depends on current GA status; keep wording conservative until confirmed by Auth SMEs).
- Whether public docs should mirror a subset of FAQ (docs team to confirm safe subset and link hygiene).

Acceptance criteria
- [x] Confluence designated as canonical for narrative content; Drive PDFs treated as exports only.
- [x] Versioning and filename conventions documented.
- [x] Quarterly review workflow defined with minimum approvers.
- [x] Access model defined (customer-shareable vs internal-only) and required labels set.
- [x] “Single latest kit link” approach defined (Confluence hub + Drive shortcut).

Related
- PM-1847 (kickoff + deliverables)
- PM-1861 (gap analysis / inventory)
- ENG-23344 (evidence pointer index refresh)
- DES-912 (one-pager formatting template)

Notes
This ticket defines the process. Asset-specific edits and publication are tracked on the individual FAQ/one-pager/RFP tasks and their associated approval comments.
